about: Pictures that play with the depth-map camera. For shots with people, cutouts records the people to separate and depthSource is an optional source map. Empty-location (depth-only) entries need no cutouts or plate: they can name a depthMap directly for --wire, or be regenerated from Depth Anything with only --depth-model. The tool writes generated paths back here; src/film/studio-edits.json (pictureLook) points the film at them.

peopleInShot.130-the-roof: Jack, Vera and the old woman
peopleInShot.206-the-window-swollen-shut: the old woman and a man
peopleInShot.207-the-pink-payphone: Jack and the man in the chair
peopleInShot.337-engine-off: Jack and Vera in the car

peopleNote: Pictures with people in them. A depth map alone stretches a person as the camera moves, so a depth entry on any of these must cut the people out (depthCutouts) and paint the gap in (depthPlate); scripts/film-depth.entry.ts fails otherwise. Add to it when a new picture with people gets depth.

cutouts.name: the man at the middle desk
the woman behind the middle desk

379-the-laundry.note: The woman on the right, half behind a sheet, stays in the plate: BiRefNet would not take her without the sheets round her, and on this drift (amount 0.09) her depth moves her about a pixel against them.

73-05-toward-the-tracks.note: Vera running away toward the tracks, small at mid-frame. Cut out (BiRefNet) with the street painted in behind her (LaMa), so the truck move does not stretch her. Until 22 October it had a depth-only map made on the belief that nobody was in shot.

75-02-the-empty-lounge.note: Depth Anything v1 ViT-S ONNX map (higher = nearer), written at the picture's exact size. Machine-made and not eyeballed against the still — check it before it ships. No people visible.
